title: Isomorphic Strings
summary: Determine if two strings s and t are isomorphic by checking if characters in s can be replaced to match t, maintaining character order and ensuring no two characters map to the same character, allowing a character to map to itself.
statement: Determine if two strings s and t are isomorphic by checking if characters in s can be replaced to match t, maintaining character order and ensuring no two characters map to the same character, allowing a character to map to itself.
constraints: s and t have equal lengths from 1 to 50000 and contain valid ASCII characters, including spaces or control characters.
Each source character maps consistently to exactly one target character, and two different source characters cannot share a target. Mapping a character to itself is allowed.
target_space_complexity: O(1) for the fixed ASCII alphabet
hints: The equality pattern of positions must be preserved in both directions.
Track a source-to-target map and a target-to-source map.
For each aligned pair, reject conflicts in either map, then record both mappings.
Equal frequency lists are not enough: aabb and abab repeat at different positions.
editorial: Two maps enforce a bijection between the characters actually encountered. A conflict in either direction invalidates the replacement rule. The independent oracle compares first-occurrence position sequences rather than character maps. This raw character-to-character contract differs from word-pattern mapping over whitespace-separated words: spaces, tabs, and control characters here are ordinary positions to map.

tests.explanation: Map e→a and g→d; both occurrences of g use the same target character.
The two o positions would need different targets, a and r, so no consistent mapping exists.
